dish: Sapporo miso ramen (the 1964 original rich-lard style)
n: Sapporo Junren, Sapporo-ten (さっぽろ純連 札幌店)
address: Hiragishi 2-jō 17-1-41, Toyohira-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: The 1964 shop that set the rich, lard-sealed Sapporo miso style — rurubu calls it the long-running origin of the modern miso bowl.

dish: yakuzen (medicinal) soup curry — 30 spices, 15 herbal extracts
n: Ajanta Yakuzen Curry Honpo Sōhonke (アジャンタ薬膳カリィ本舗総本家)
address: Kita 23-jō Higashi 20-2-18, Higashi-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Ajanta's 1970s medicinal curry is where Sapporo soup curry began; this is the head shop.

n: Soup Curry Yellow (スープカリーイエロー)
address: Elm Bldg 1F, Minami 3-jō Nishi 1-12-19, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A 1996 soup-curry house with a clear pork-and-chicken stock and a 20-step heat scale.

n: Chūgoku Ryōri Hotei (中国料理 布袋)
address: Minami 1-jō Nishi 9-1-3, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Ask Sapporo where to eat zangi and this Chinese diner comes up: fist-sized pieces fried in three oils at three temperatures.

dish: Chitose-tsuru junmai — brewery-only and seasonal sake, tasting counter
n: Chitose-tsuru Sake Museum (千歳鶴 酒ミュージアム)
address: Minami 3-jō Higashi 5-1, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: The shop and small museum of Sapporo's only sake brewery (Nihon Seishu), with free tasting counter and brewery-only bottles.

dish: Snow Royal ice cream and milk parfaits (since 1961)
n: Snow Brand Parlor Sapporo Honten (雪印パーラー 札幌本店)
address: Taiyō Seimei Sapporo Bldg 1F, Kita 2-jō Nishi 3-1-31, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Sapporo's 1961 dairy parlour: 30-plus parfaits and the 'Snow Royal' ice cream first made for a 1968 imperial visit.

n: Sapporo Senshūan Honten (札幌千秋庵 本店)
address: Minami 3-jō Nishi 3, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Confectioner since 1921, maker of the Northman bean-paste pie and Yama-oyaji biscuits.

dish: European-style dark-roast blends and house cake
n: Miyakoshiya Coffee Honten, Maruyama (宮越屋珈琲 本店)
address: Minami 2-jō Nishi 28, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Sapporo's best-known kissaten roaster; the first-floor windows look onto Maruyama Park.

dish: seasonal Hokkaido fruit and vegetable cocktails (haskap & lavender on potato shochu)
n: the bar nano.femto, Susukino
address: Near Susukino Crossing, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A 16-seat cocktail counter whose idea is 'cocktails as liquid cooking', built on Hokkaido produce.

n: Do Ermitage, Susukino (ドゥ・エルミタアヂュ)
address: Minami 3-jō Nishi 4 Bldg 10F, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: An old-school authentic bar run by a woman with about 50 years behind the counter; more than 400 whiskies.

dish: jingisukan — Roaring Forties lamb, fresh lamb shoulder
n: Jingisukan Yōyōtei Sapporo Honten (ジンギスカン羊々亭 札幌本店)
address: Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Specialist lamb grill known for its rare 'Roaring Forties' lamb.

dish: fresh-lamb jingisukan with apple-aged sauce (Otaru Keishōen recipe, 1956)
n: Nama-Ramu Jingisukan Yamagoya, Susukino (生ラムジンギスカン 山小屋)
address: Dai-5 Green Bldg 1F, Minami 4-jō Nishi 4-13-2, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Susukino fresh-lamb grill carrying on the 1956 sauce of Otaru's Keishōen.

n: Beer Bar North Island (ビアバー ノースアイランド)
address: Large Country Bldg 10F, Minami 2-jō Nishi 4-10-1, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Taproom of Sapporo's North Island Beer (founded 2003, now brewed in Ebetsu) — fresh kegs, guest and seasonal beers.

n: Moon and Sun Brewing (月と太陽BREWING)
address: Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A brewpub on the city's craft-beer trail.

n: Misoramen Senmonten Ōkami Soup (味噌らーめん専門店 狼スープ)
address: Near Nakajima Park, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Started as a yatai in 2000 and reopened in 2012; it serves miso ramen only.

n: Kiraito, Tanukikōji (喜来登)
address: Minami 2-jō Nishi 6, Chuo-ku, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A Tanukikōji miso ramen shop that fries the vegetables and garlic in the wok before the soup goes in, the old Sapporo way.

n: Otaru Wine Gallery — Hokkaido Wine Otaru Winery (北海道ワイン おたるワインギャラリー)
address: Asarigawa Onsen 1-130, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Hokkaido Wine's head winery (founded 1974): a tasting bar with about 100 wines and paid winery tours.

n: Soba-ya Yabuhan, Otaru (蕎麦屋 籔半)
address: Inaho 2-19-14, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A 1954 Edo-style soba house near Otaru Station.

dish: house ice cream made the 1919 way
n: Ice Cream Parlor Misono, Otaru (アイスクリームパーラー美園)
address: Inaho 2-12-15, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Opened in 1919 as the first shop in Hokkaido to sell ice cream, and still uses its original method.

n: Uomasa, Otaru (魚真)
address: Inaho 2-5-11, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Local-catch sushi at fair prices, as popular with residents as with visitors.

dish: Yoichi estate wine and vineyard lunch
n: OcciGabi Winery, Yoichi (オチガビワイナリー)
address: Yamada-chō 635, Yoichi, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Founded in 2012 by the Ochii couple, who want to make Yoichi Japan's leading wine town. Tasting counter, terrace and a restaurant overlooking the vines.

n: Yoichi Winery (余市ワイナリー)
address: Kurokawa-chō 1318, Yoichi, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Makes its wine only from grapes grown and pressed in Yoichi, and runs a lunch restaurant on site.

dish: award-winning cool-climate wine; vineyard lunch and dinner
n: NIKI Hills Winery, Niki (NIKI Hills Winery)
address: Asahidai 148-1, Niki, Yoichi District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A hilltop winery with lodging above the Yoichi River valley, whose cool-climate wines have won international awards.

n: Otaru Milk Plant (小樽ミルクプラント)
address: Hanazono 2-12-13, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Otaru's oldest soft-serve stand, run by Hoshō Gyūnyū in its 1936 milk-plant office.

dish: cream zenzai and coffee in a Meiji merchant house
n: Taishō Glass Kuboya, Sakaimachi (大正硝子 くぼ家)
address: Sakaimachi 4-4, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A kissaten in the historic former Sakaiya shop on Sakaimachi Street, kept going by Taishō Glass.

n: Kita no Donburiya Takinami Shokudō, Sankaku Market (北のどんぶり屋 滝波食堂)
address: Sankaku Market, Inaho 3-10-16, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
w: The Takinami fish shop's diner in the Triangle Market — seafood from the tanks onto a pick-your-own bowl, with a queue every day.

n: New Sankō, Otaru (ニュー三幸)
address: Sun Mall 1-bangai, Inaho 1-3-6, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A 1954 all-round restaurant, now known for its ankake yakisoba on house egg noodles. Bunkacho has named the dish a '100-Year Food'.

n: Otaru Ankake Yakisoba Kakuryū (小樽あんかけ焼きそば 鶴龍)
address: Otaru Dejō Kōji, Ironai 1-1, Otaru, Hokkaido, Japan
w: An ankake-yakisoba specialist in the Dejō Kōji food alley by the canal.

n: Kakizaki Shōten Kaisen Kōbō, Yoichi (柿崎商店 海鮮工房)
address: Kurokawa-chō 7-25, Yoichi, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A seafood wholesaler's fish market with a second-floor diner, four minutes from JR Yoichi; queues at weekends.

dish: Hi-no-Ho craft gin from home-grown botanicals
n: Shakotan Blue Distillery — Shakotan Spirit (積丹ブルー蒸溜所)
address: Nozuka-chō Uento 229-1, Shakotan, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A 'farm family distillery' growing about 100 botanicals on 5.7 ha for its Hi-no-Ho gins.
